text: The LORD said to Moses:
"Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to lift the censers out of the smoldering fire and scatter the coals far away, for the censers are holy.

Take the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives and hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for they were presented before the LORD and have become holy. They shall be a sign to the Israelites."
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned had presented, and they were hammered out as an overlay for the altar,

a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not of Aaron's line, should ever come near to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his company—just as the LORD had spoken to Eleazar through Moses.

versions.text: a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not of Aaron's line, should ever come near to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his company—just as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
versions.explanation: The final לוֹ ("to him") is not represented in the translation; the word specifies the addressee of the LORD's word, namely Eleazar, who is the subject of the preceding narrative.

text: But the next day the whole community of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron. "You have killed the LORD's people," they said.
And as the assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and there was the cloud covering it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Then Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
And the LORD said to Moses:
"Get away from this assembly, so that I may consume them in an instant." And they fell facedown.

Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer, put fire on it from the altar and lay incense on it, then hurry to the assembly and make atonement for them. Wrath has gone out from the LORD; the plague has begun."
Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly. The plague had indeed begun among the people, but he put in the incense and made atonement for the people.

versions.text: Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly. The plague had indeed begun among the people, but he put on the incense and made atonement for them.
versions.explanation: "Put on the incense" is awkward English (it reads as putting on clothing); the censer receives the incense. Also, the Hebrew ends with "for the people" (עַל־הָעָם), which is more concrete than the pronoun "them" and rounds off the sentence better for oral reading.

text: He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
Fourteen thousand seven hundred died in the plague, besides those who had died in the affair of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and the plague had been stopped.

versions.text: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, for the plague had been stopped.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is a simple circumstantial clause joined by waw ("and the plague had been stopped"), not a causal statement. "For" wrongly makes the stopping of the plague the reason Aaron returned.

text: The LORD said to Moses:

"Speak to the Israelites and get a staff from each of them, one for every ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff,
and write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, since there is to be one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
Place them in the tent of meeting in front of the ark of the testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid myself of this constant grumbling of the Israelites against you."
So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders brought him a staff, one for each ancestral house—twelve staffs in all—and Aaron's staff was among them.
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
The next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron's staff, the staff of the house of Levi: it had sprouted, put out buds, blossomed, and produced ripe almonds.
Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took back his own staff.

The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's staff back in front of the ark of the testimony, to be kept as a warning sign to these rebels. This will put an end to their grumbling against me, so that they will not die."
So Moses did it; just as the LORD commanded him, so he did.

versions.text: Moses did just as the LORD commanded him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a deliberate double statement ("Moses did... so he did"), an emphatic formula of obedience that the current rendering flattens. Restoring the repetition preserves both the emphasis and the closing cadence for oral reading.

text: The Israelites said to Moses, "Look, we are dying! We are lost, all of us are lost!
Anyone who so much as comes near the LORD's dwelling will die. Are we all to perish?"
